method: Hand review of the 63 keyword-positive failing reports in the 246-report corpus. Positive means the report recomputes or disputes a numerical relationship, including denominator, subtotal completeness and category-dependent aggregation. Calendar weekday derivation is included; unsupported chronology without recomputation is excluded. These broader semantic cases remain labelled misses rather than being silently removed from recall.
negative_review_notes: Other candidate reports concern attribution, missing legal exceptions, changing statuses, publication versus effective dates, or scope; numbers appearing in those findings are not themselves miscomputed.
Fraud r3 explicitly holds the one-percent-of-one-billion arithmetic; r11/r12 concern who qualifies for the 120-day exception, not elapsed-day arithmetic.
Iran bases r6 lacks the war-start date in cited evidence; r7 holds the underlying dates and disputes direct quotation. Neither establishes a wrong four-month calculation.
California r9 holds both percentages and disputes who supplied the birthplace entries.
KPMG r1 channels disputes whether banknotes were distributed, not the sum itself; vendor-energy instead explicitly recomputes the category subtotal and is retained below.
KPMG r4 holds the 57.4-million subtotal but disputes the description of one payment; Vitol r4/r5 hold donation sums and dispute recipient/donor classification.
